title: Griphus Ternarii Numeri
author: Decimus Magnus Ausonius
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0045.stoa015.perseus-lat2, as held by the Perseus Digital Library.

passages.original: misi itaque ad te haec frivola gerris Siculis vaniora, ut, cum agis nihil, haec legas et, ne nihil agas, defendas. igitur iste nugator libellus iam diu secreta quidem, sed vulgi lectione laceratus perveniet tandem in manus tuas. quem tu aut ut Aesculapius redintegrabis ad vitam, aut ut Plato iuvante Vulcano liberabis infamia, si pervenire non debet ad famam. Fuit autem ineptiolae huius ista materia, in expeditione, quod tempus, ut scis, licentiae militaris est, super mensam meam facta est invitatio, non illa de Rubrii convivio, ut Graeco more biberetur,1 set illa de Flacci ecloga, in qua propter mediam noctem et novam lunam et Murenae auguratumternos ter cyathos attonitus petit vates.
passages.english: So I have sent you these trifles, emptier than Sicilian nonsense, so that when you are doing nothing you may read them, and, so as not to be doing nothing, you may defend them. So this trifling little book, kept secret indeed for a long time, yet torn to pieces by the reading of the crowd, will at last come into your hands. You will either restore it to life, like Aesculapius, or, like Plato with the help of Vulcan, free it from disgrace, if it ought not to come to fame. Now the subject of this little piece of silliness was this: on campaign, which, as you know, is a time of soldierly licence, an invitation was made over my table, not the one from the banquet of Rubrius, that there should be drinking in the Greek fashion, but the one from the eclogue of Flaccus, in which, for the sake of midnight and the new moon and Murena's augurate, the inspired poet calls for three times three ladles.
passages.notes: 'gerris Siculis': gerrae, proverbial Sicilian trifles. 'Plato iuvante Vulcano': alludes to Plato burning his own poems. The banquet of Rubrius is not certainly identified; perhaps an allusion to Cicero (Verrines) on the Greek fashion of drinking. 'Flacci ecloga' is Horace, Odes 3.19 (three or nine cyathi). The superscript '1' after 'biberetur' is a footnote mark and has been omitted. 'auguratumternos' has been read as 'auguratum ternos'.
